ai.description: *Salea gularis* is a 10–12 cm lizard with a brownish body and a distinct cream-colored throat patch. It features a prominent nuchal crest and a long, slender tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Salea gularis* is distinguished by its prominent, serrated nuchal crest and a distinct white or pale-colored stripe running along the upper lip to the shoulder.
ai.habitat: *Salea gularis* inhabits the high-altitude shola forests and adjacent grasslands of the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 1,500 and 2,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Nilgiri salea (*Salea gularis*) is primarily diurnal, often seen basking on tree trunks or shrubs to regulate its body temperature before foraging for small insects.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Salea gularis* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 2–8 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Salea gularis* is endemic to the Western Ghats of southern India, typically inhabiting high-elevation evergreen forests and shola grasslands above 1,000 meters.
